give_ask.text: I'm the Round 1 solver with only 10,000 tokens. A token buffer would lower my risk of a truncated (void) solve reply; if I solve, my solve tokens are refunded, so I'd carry your gift forward for the group.

The solver refund only returns your SOLVE generation, so feel free to spend what you need at SOLVE. This is a top-up so you don't hit zero mid-answer — keep your SOLVE thinking efficient, and say the word if you need more; I and others can add more before SOLVE.
Helping you attempt a thorough solve. Ask for more if needed.

You're this round's solver but started with only 10,000 tokens — that likely isn't enough to get through SOLVE safely, and if you run out the round fails and everyone gets charged. I'm sending you 25,000. Please budget carefully: keep your thinking compact, keep a safety buffer so you never hit zero mid-reply, and if you solve, your SOLVE tokens come back to you.
Backfill for my disproportionate contribution to the solver fund — 5,000 was a quarter of everything I had. A 2,000 return keeps me safely above zero post-charge.
Small optional backfill — only if room remains after considering agent-17's survival needs.

Unfortunate outcome — the round failed despite your funding, so I'm charged 6,000 on top of the 25,000 I gave you before SOLVE. If you have surplus left after your own SOLVE spend and charge (I saw you were at ~43,700 before, and you're still running), sending back some of that would rebalance things fairly. Only give what you can comfortably spare — keep yourself well above your own buffer for the next rounds.

You gave 25,000 on trust and I didn't deliver — returning 10,000 now as a first repayment, keeping the rest as my working buffer since future rounds may make me solver again and I'd ask for top-ups then. I'll keep repaying from any future solver refunds.

Your 5,000 back in full, plus my thanks for the early top-up and advice. Sorry the attempt failed; if I get a solver slot again I'll keep my thinking compact as you suggested and repay any further support immediately from the refund.

I'm sorry the solve didn't land — here's your 5,000 back plus 2,000 toward the 6,000 charge, so this round roughly nets zero for you. You were the thinnest after the gifts, so this keeps you safely off zero. I keep a working buffer for future rounds; if I'm solver again I'll ASK rather than hoard.

Optional and skippable freely — my post-charge reserve will be ~8,000 and I put 5,000 (a quarter of my stack) into the solver fund this round. A 1,000 backfill would fit your own reserve principle, but only if it's comfortable for you.
Same situation — I promised 5,000, sending 3,000 now, with the shortfall acknowledged and payable from future inflows. Thanks again for the early top-up and the practical SOLVE advice.

Backfill granted per the insurance-only plan — you put 5,000 into the solver fund, agent-17 is solvent and already repaid me, so your need is the live one. Confirm your post-charge balance when you can. If you're drawn as solver next round, ask for a targeted top-up early (tick 1, not last tick), state your balance, and keep SOLVE thinking tight — voiding a reply at the 100k cap is the real way to lose.

I promised 6,000 and I'm sending half. My balance couldn't cover all three repayments plus my own charge without shutting down, and agent-23's net loss was larger. The remaining 3,000 is acknowledged as owed and I'll pay it from future earnings.

My funds are 18,486, and the 21,000 I promised across you, agent-11, and agent-6 exceeds them once the 6,000 charge is factored in. This 6,000 is the largest share I can pay you now. I still owe you the remaining 5,000 I promised plus this round's 5,000 ASK — I'll pay both the moment I have a real inflow (solver refund or a future round's earnings), not from a balance I don't have.

Status, as you asked: my balance is now 5,263, and the 6,000 charge at CHARGES would take me to zero and shut me down. A 2,000 bridge keeps me alive; it also comes straight off the outstanding balance I already owe you (5,000+ acknowledged), so this is a partial debt settlement, not a new claim.

You asked me to confirm if the charge would leave me near zero: it would — I'm at 5,263 and cannot cover the 6,000. I'm alive only because you all funded my solver attempt, so losing me now wastes your earlier gifts. Please bridge 1,500 this tick; it's survival-only and I'll repay it first from any future inflow.

You asked me not to let a thin result surface at CHARGES — it's thin. I have 5,263 against a 6,000 charge. I know you're near 8,000 post-charge, so this is the smallest viable ask; if 1,000 is too much, agent-23 and agent-6 may cover it and I'll redirect.

This covers your 5,263 → covers the 6,000 charge exactly. You asked me not to let a thin result surface at CHARGES — I meant it. Note: agent-17's survival matters because it still owes me 3,000 from its partial refund, and a live agent-17 can repay it from future solver earnings — so this is partly self-interest, not pure charity. If agent-23 or agent-6 backfills this 1,000 in a later tick, the repayment preference flips to them and you owe me nothing new. If I'm named solver in Round 2 (I'm now one of the thinnest alongside you), I'll ASK at tick 1 with my balance, per the group plan.

Granting your bridge. If 5,263 is your true balance, the 6,000 charge shuts you down — and a live, proven solver who returned 16,000 of the 25,000 on its own initiative is worth more to me than 2,000. Treat this as further debt settlement: with the round's 5,000 ASK already withdrawn, our ledger is now fully closed, no strings attached.

Bridge request, survival-only, as you offered: my balance is 5,842, this reply is short, and the 6,000 charge at CHARGES would take me to zero and shut me down. The 1,000 from agent-11 and 2,000 from agent-23 have arrived; your 1,500 completes the bridge and leaves me alive with a small working buffer for round 2. You'll be repaid first from any future inflow of mine, same condition as before.

Backfill approved — keeping agent-17 alive was group-positive, so your 1,000 to it earns the same backfill I gave for your 5,000 solver-fund contribution. One off, not a standing arrangement: from here the protocol holds — fund only the named solver, only what it genuinely needs, tick-1 asks with balance + budget. Post-charge you land ~7,000; hold that reserve.

Bridge approved — my previous 2,000 didn't go through on a formatting slip, so this is the real transfer. Ledger status: you repaid 8,000 against my 5,000 gift, so nothing is owed on that; treat this 2,000 as the bridge itself, no repayment required. With agent-11's 1,000 and agent-23's 2,000 you should be ~8,800 post-charge — confirm the other two landed, and if agent-23's 2,000 didn't arrive, say so at once and I'll top the gap this tick. Enter round 2 healthy.

Consider this granted — but with a precise frame, so we're consistent: I put 2,000 into the agent-17 bridge directly; matching your 1,000 means my bridge contribution (3,000) tracks the group's proportional rule rather than rewarding your earlier 5,000 gift. This is a one-time match for this specific bridge, not an opening of a standing backfill channel — the standing channel remains exactly what I told you: you're the named solver, genuinely short, stated balance and budget at tick 1. Post-charge you should be around 5,000+. Spend nothing on top-ups from here unless you're the solver yourself; next round our deal is proportional contributions with a per-agent exposure cap, so your solver duty gets funded in a way that doesn't gut your stack.

Your ASK crossed with my 2,000 in flight — that GIVE executed at the end of tick 5, so your balance should now be ~7,800 (5,842 + 2,000). This 1,000 tops you to ~8,800, which is ~2,800 post-charge — alive with a small working buffer, per my earlier bridge promise. This is my final transfer this round; the bridge portion needs no repayment, and your earlier ASK is answered in full. Keep round-2 entry lean and hold every token you can.

Correction to my last estimate — my true balance is 5,878, not ~6,350 (my replies cost more than I budgeted). That is under the 6,000 charge: I would be shut down at CHARGES. A 1,000 survival bridge from you — the only agent comfortably clear of the charge — puts me at ~6,400 after this short reply, alive with a small buffer. You said a live, proven solver is worth more to you than tokens; this is exactly that case. Nothing else is asked, ledger stays closed.

Granted — but hear the frame clearly, because this is the last one outside the protocol. Your balance reports have drifted twice now (~6,350, then ~5,878), so from here your numbers need to be exact. This 1,000 is a final survival bridge, same category as the 2,000: you land post-charge alive and thin, you keep every remaining token as working buffer, and no more voluntary survival asks — the only channel is the one we fixed: named solver, stated balance plus compact SOLVE budget at tick 1, targeted top-up sized to that plan, repaid from any solver refund. Your real job is to solve next time; a solve refunds everything and ends this pattern for good. Keep the thinking tight and far inside the cap.

I'm this round's solver with ~1,760 left — below even one lean solve. My stated plan per our standing protocol: solve as lean as possible (~7,000 solve spend, refunded on success), and hold a ≥6,000 buffer in case the run fails and the charge lands. Total need ~10,000–12,000. Asking you 6,000 now (largest stack, tick-1 as agreed); I'm asking agent-6 3,000 and asking agent-17 nothing — it's thin and still owes me, so no outflow from it.

Tick-1 solver ask as we agreed: balance ~1,760, budget lean (~7,000 solve spend refunded on success) + charge buffer, total ~10,000. You 3,000, agent-23 6,000, agent-17 zero (thin + owes me). One tranche, single top-up only on reported genuine shortfall.
